newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak trade deficit widens as imports surge.
newsitem.headline: Slovak trade deficit widens as imports surge.

text.p: Slovakia's foreign trade deficit continued to widen in November, boosted mainly by an increase in imports of cars, fossil fuels and nuclear plant technology, the Statistical Bureau (SUSR) said on Tuesday.
SUSR said the trade deficit for the first 11 months of 1996 totalled 44.82 billion crowns, up from a shortfall of 42.52 billion crowns for the January-October period.
In the first 11 months of 1995, Slovakia posted a trade deficit of only 2.64 billion crowns.

Overall exports for January-November totalled 247.54 billion crowns, 5.5 percent more than in the same period of the previous year. Imports rose by 59.19 billion crowns, or 25 percent, year-on-year, totalling 296.36 billion crowns.
At the heart of the deficit's expansion were imports of fossil fuels and mineral oils, accounting for 50 billion crowns and showing a year-on-year increase of 22.9 percent.

Nuclear power plant equipment for the reconstruction of the Jaslovske Bohunice, the only nuclear plant currently operating in the country, and for the completion of the Mochovce power station totalled 45.1 billion crowns for the period, a rise of 25.7 percent over the same period in 1995.
The fastest growth among imports was in most types of motor vehicles, rising 142 percent year-on-year and accounting for 29.4 billion crowns.
Major export articles were iron and rolled steel, accounting for 34.1 billion crowns, a decrease of 11 percent compared with the first 11 months of 1995.
The Czech Republic remained Slovakia's leading trading partner, accounting for 25.2 percent of overall imports and for 31.2 percent of all exports.

Germany and Austria followed with 21.1 and 6.1 percent share in Slovak exports, respectively. The second and third largest import volumes came from Russia and Germany, accounting for 17.4 and 14.5 percent, respectively.
Trade with OECD countries produced a 15.54 billion crown deficit, up from a 13.554 billion crowns shortfall in the first 10 months of the year.

The trade deficit with Russia widened in November by 4.33 billion crowns to total 42.87 billion crowns. Meanwhile, Slovakia's trade with the EU countries ended with a deficit of 5.89 billion, compared with a surplus of 5.91 billion crowns in January-November period of 1995.
